---

Dark mode is enabled by providing dark and light to theme in the `_quarto.yml` file.

The default toggle is very small, it's been customised from [following advice on GitHub](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/discussions/7924#discussioncomment-7987263).....

::: {.dark-test}
DARK TEST SHOULD BE ORANGE
:::

::: {.light-test}
LIGHT TEST SHOULD BE YELLOW
:::

### No crossref or caption
```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Parameters for the normal distribution
mean = 0
std_dev = 1
x = np.linspace(mean - 4*std_dev, mean + 4*std_dev, 1000)
y_light = (1/(std_dev * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi))) * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - mean) / std_dev)**2)
y_dark = -(1/(std_dev * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi))) * np.exp(-0.5 * ((x - mean) / std_dev)**2)

# Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
plt.plot(x, y_light, label='LIGHT MODE')
plt.title('LIGHT MODE')
plt.show()

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
plt.plot(x, y_dark, label='DARK MODE')
plt.title('DARK MODE')
plt.show()
```

# Accessing colours from brand palette

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
from brand_yml import Brand
brand_light = Brand.from_yaml("../../_brand-light.yml")
brand_dark = Brand.from_yaml("../../_brand-dark.yml")
brand_light.color.palette['light-mode-primary']

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
plt.plot(x, y_light, label='LIGHT MODE', color=brand_light.color.palette['light-mode-primary'])
plt.title('LIGHT MODE')
plt.show()

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
plt.plot(x, y_dark, label='DARK MODE', color=brand_dark.color.palette['dark-mode-primary'])
plt.title('DARK MODE')
plt.show()
```
